entries.headline: Goldgroup completes C$101 million strategic investment in Luca Mining
entries.dek: Goldgroup Mining acquired subscription receipts expected to convert into roughly 19.9% of Luca Mining once its Cozamin Mine acquisition closes.
entries.caption: Goldgroup Mining's new stake in Luca Mining is tied to Luca's pending acquisition of the Cozamin Mine.

sources.title: Goldgroup Completes Strategic Investment in Luca Mining

unverified_claims: Goldgroup's expected resulting stake of approximately 19.9% of Luca is the company's own stated figure, pending completion of the Cozamin Mine acquisition and conversion of the subscription receipts.
The characterization of the transaction as a 'strategic investment' is Goldgroup's own description.
brief: Goldgroup Mining Inc. (TSXV: GORO) (NYSE American: GORO) said it completed a C$101,123,662 strategic investment in Luca Mining Corp., acquiring 101,123,662 subscription receipts at C$1.00 each. The receipts were part of a bought-deal private placement Luca is conducting in connection with its proposed acquisition of the Cozamin Mine, which closed October 14, 2026.

The subscription receipts convert into common shares of Luca once release conditions are satisfied, including completion of the Cozamin Mine acquisition. Goldgroup said it may elect early conversion, provided its resulting stake does not exceed 19.9% without further approvals. Following conversion, Goldgroup is expected to hold about 19.9% of Luca on a non-diluted basis.

Goldgroup secured an investor rights agreement entitling it, while holding at least 10% of Luca's shares, to participate in future equity financings, top up its holdings against dilutive issuances, and nominate two directors to Luca's board. The release does not disclose the total size of Luca's offering, Luca's ticker symbol, or the terms of the Cozamin Mine acquisition itself.
body: Goldgroup Mining Inc. (TSXV: GORO) (NYSE American: GORO) said it completed a C$101,123,662 strategic investment in Luca Mining Corp. on October 14, 2026, acquiring 101,123,662 subscription receipts at a price of C$1.00 per receipt. The receipts were issued as part of a bought-deal private placement that Luca is conducting in connection with its proposed acquisition of the Cozamin Mine, which the release refers to as the "Cozamin Acquisition" without further describing its terms.

A subscription receipt is a security that converts into a common share once specified conditions are met, rather than granting share ownership immediately. Here, the receipts convert into Luca common shares once release conditions are satisfied, which the release says include completion of the Cozamin Acquisition. Goldgroup said it may elect to convert its receipts early, provided doing so would not take its holding above 19.9% of Luca's outstanding shares without further approval.

Following conversion, Goldgroup said it will hold 101,123,662 Luca common shares, representing approximately 19.9% of Luca's outstanding shares on a non-diluted basis. The release does not state Luca's total share count on a diluted basis, nor does it give the total size of the bought-deal offering of which Goldgroup's receipts were a part.

Goldgroup also secured an investor rights agreement with Luca. While Goldgroup holds at least 10% of Luca's shares, the agreement gives it the right to participate in future equity financings and top up its holding in relation to dilutive issuances, and the right to nominate two persons to Luca's board of directors.

The release states that Goldgroup "intends to assess opportunities relating to its investment in Luca" and that, depending on its strategic priorities, market conditions and its evaluation of Luca's business, it may acquire additional securities, exercise its board nomination rights, or dispose of some or all of its position.

The release does not name Luca's stock ticker or exchange, does not name any underwriter or agent for Luca's offering, and does not describe the terms of the Cozamin Mine acquisition — the price, the seller, or Luca's other obligations — beyond referring to it as a pending acquisition that conversion of the receipts is conditioned on.
Goldgroup's contacts for the release are listed as Javier Reyes, chief executive officer, and Sophia Shane, in corporate development.

entries.headline: US consumer prices rose 0.6% in September
entries.dek: The Bureau of Labor Statistics said core prices, excluding food and energy, rose 0.3% on the month and 2.6% over the year.
entries.caption: The Consumer Price Index rose 0.6% in September, driven largely by a 9.1% monthly increase in gasoline prices, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said.

sources.title: CPI for all items increases 0.6% in September; gasoline rises

brief: The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics said the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers rose 0.6% in September on a seasonally adjusted basis, and 3.7% over the 12 months ending in September, not seasonally adjusted. The index for items excluding food and energy rose 0.3% in September and 2.6% over the year.

The bureau said the gasoline index rose 9.1% in September, "accounting for over half of the monthly all items increase." Over the year, it said the energy index rose 20.4%, "due in large part to the index for gasoline rising 34.2 percent."

The shelter index rose 0.4% in September after rising 0.3% in August, and is up 3.2% over the year, the bureau said. The food index was unchanged in September on a seasonally adjusted basis but rose 2.5% over the year.
body: The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers rose 0.6 percent in September 2026 on a seasonally adjusted basis. Over the 12 months ending in September, the index rose 3.7 percent on a not-seasonally-adjusted basis, the bureau said.

The index for all items less food and energy — commonly referred to as core CPI — rose 0.3 percent in September on a seasonally adjusted basis, and was up 2.6 percent over the year, not seasonally adjusted, according to the release.

The bureau attributed much of the monthly increase to energy prices, stating that "the index for gasoline rose 9.1 percent in September, accounting for over half of the monthly all items increase." Over the 12-month period, it said "the energy index increased 20.4 percent... due in large part to the index for gasoline rising 34.2 percent."
Shelter costs continued to rise: the bureau said "the shelter index rose 0.4 percent in September after rising 0.3 percent in August," with the shelter index up 3.2 percent over the year.
The food index was unchanged in September on a seasonally adjusted basis, the bureau said, though it rose 2.5 percent over the preceding 12 months.
The release reports the measured price changes for the month and the year; it includes no assessment of future price trends or monetary policy.

entries.headline: HawkEye 360 secures $36 million in new international contracts
entries.dek: The Q3 awards span more than 10 allied and partner nations across the Indo-Pacific, Middle East, Europe and the Americas, the company said.
entries.caption: HawkEye 360, a signals-intelligence company listed on the NYSE, reports new defense contracts spanning allied nations across four world regions.

sources.title: HawkEye 360 Secures $36 million in New International Contracts Driven by Increasing Demand for Signals Intelligence

unverified_claims: HawkEye 360's description of itself as 'the global leader in signals intelligence data and analytics' rests only on the company's own characterization.
The characterization of customers' security environments as 'increasingly complex' is the company's own description.
brief: HawkEye 360, Inc. (NYSE: HAWK) said it secured $36 million in new international contracts during the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. The company described itself as "the global leader in signals intelligence data and analytics," and said the awards span more than 10 allied and partner nations.

The release groups the new multi-year awards by region: customers in the Indo-Pacific, Middle East, Europe and the Americas. HawkEye 360 said these customers are turning to its radio-frequency data and analytics for situational awareness, threat identification and operational decision-making. No individual contracts, countries or customers are named, and the $36 million figure is not broken down.

Chief executive John Serafini said the awards "reflect the growing recognition among allied nations that signals intelligence is essential to modern defense operations." The release gives no revenue or backlog figures beyond the $36 million in new awards, and does not state when the contracted work will be delivered or recognized as revenue.
body: HawkEye 360, Inc. (NYSE: HAWK) announced on October 15, 2026 that it secured $36 million in new international contracts during the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. The release describes HawkEye 360 as "the global leader in signals intelligence data and analytics" and says the new awards reflect demand for its capabilities across more than 10 allied and partner nations.

The release structures the new business as multi-year awards rather than one-time contracts, though it does not state the length of the multi-year terms or break the $36 million figure down by region, country or individual award. It groups the customers by region: the Indo-Pacific, the Middle East, Europe and the Americas.

HawkEye 360 said these defense and intelligence customers are turning to its data and analytics "to strengthen situational awareness, identify emerging threats, and support timely operational decision-making" as they face what the company describes as increasingly complex security environments.

The company's business, per its own description in the release, is built on detecting, geolocating and characterizing radio-frequency emissions worldwide from space-based collection, which it combines with proprietary signal processing and AI-powered analytics to produce what it calls domain awareness and early-warning indicators for the U.S. government and allied partners.

Chief executive John Serafini said: "these awards reflect the growing recognition among allied nations that signals intelligence is essential to modern defense operations." He added that the company's focus remains on delivering capabilities that give "Warfighters and decision-makers" the information they need to understand the operational environment and act with confidence.

The release names no specific country, government agency or company as a customer, and identifies no individual contract. It gives no revenue or backlog figures beyond the $36 million in new awards, and does not state a timetable for when the contracted work will be delivered or recognized as revenue.
